issue_context.title: Preemption logic on PDB violations
issue_context.body:
In one recent fix (#91986), we enhanced the preemption logic to respect `pdb.Status.DisruptedPods`. But there is a glitch:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ef8380e6c0ada9ef682d2d3566cbb16b79445233/pkg/scheduler/core/generic_scheduler_test.go#L1486-L1502

- if we changed the DisruptedPods  in L1499 from "a" to "b", the test would fail
- it would also fail if we change the pods (i.e., []Pod{"b", "a"}) ordering in L1496~L1497

This is a problem we need to fix.

---

On the other hand, I'm thinking about the real semantics of `pdb.Status.DisruptedPods`. According to the docs, if a pod is matched by the "DisruptedPods" list, it denotes the pod is about to be evicted by API server as it at least has violated one disruption budget. Given this fact, IMO in scheduler preemption, we should treat this kind of pod as "nonViolating" in all cases - no matter the current `pdb.Status.DisruptionsAllowed` is negative or not. So that the scheduler would treat them as preemption candidates.

/sig scheduling
